proof: Absorption: walk a straight segment from a point of codeword 124 to a point of codeword 156. Every possible sequence of codewords along it breaks one of the rules that convex regions must follow (each region meets a line in one interval; Prabhakar's absorption lemma), so no convex drawing exists.

Split-cover pinch: neuron 1's region is covered by two groups {2, 4} and {3, 5, 6}; a segment from codeword 124 to codeword 156 inside it must pass where both groups overlap, which forces a contradiction between regions 4, 6 and 3 (Prabhakar's pinch lemma).

proof: Six-Role Wall: no codeword contains 1, 3 and 5 together, so in the plane a line separates region 1 from the overlap of 3 and 5. Sets 2 and 6 cover the rest of 3 and 5, and region 4 bridges the line. In each of the three possible left-to-right orders of 3, 5 and 4 along the line, some region is forced to enter, leave and re-enter a straight line, or 4 is forced into a region it never meets.

Forced-Facet Descent: put three points in codewords 124, 345, 156. Every codeword the code forces onto segments between them, and between those, is reached, including all five maximal ones, so any convex drawing restricted to the plane through the three points is still a full drawing. So if this code were convex it would be convex in the plane, which the wall rules out.
